newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sino-British Joint Declaration on HK at a glance.
newsitem.headline: Sino-British Joint Declaration on HK at a glance.

text.p: On December 19, 1984 then British prime minister Margaret Thatcher and then Chinese premier Zhao Ziyang signed the Joint Declaration sealing the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule.
Following are highlights of the treaty which was registered at the United Nations by both countries on June 12, 1985 -
** Britain will return Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30, 1997
** From July 1, 1997, Hong Kong will be a a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China
** Hong Kong will enjoy a high degree of autonomy under a "One Country, Two Systems" policy
** Hong Kong's capitalist system and lifestyle will remain unchanged for 50 years
** China's socialist system and policies will not be practised in Hong Kong
** Hong Kong will be governed by Hong Kong people and not by officials sent from China by Beijing
** Hong Kong will retain its separate legal, fiscal, monetary and social system
** Its free market economic policies and cosmopolitan lifestyle will remain intact
** The top 23 Civil Service positions must be held by Chinese citizens who must have lived in Hong Kong for 15 years and who do not have right of abode elsewhere
** Foreign nationals in the civil service will be permitted to continue in their posts, but cannot occupy one of the top 23 positions
